title: WE MUST ADD STRUCTURE TO DEEP LEARNING BECAUSE...
summary: Conversation arguing that current deep learning is too dependent on scale, memorization, and opaque heuristics. The speakers propose category theory, type-like structure, and domain-specific ML languages as a path toward more compositional, explainable, and verifiable neural architectures.
claims: Current deep learning practice relies too heavily on scale, memorization, and ad hoc engineering rather than principled structure.
Category theory offers a way to abstract away irrelevant detail and reason about compositional structure across machine learning architectures.
A practical outcome of this research direction is the design of domain-specific languages for machine learning with clearer semantics and better human intelligibility.
Type-driven or semantics-aware ML systems could make neural modules more compositional, verifiable, and useful for higher-order engineering tasks.
Present transformer-style language models do not robustly learn recursion, which limits their suitability for serious software engineering and other algorithmic tasks.
Neural networks are not necessarily barred in principle from Turing-complete computation, but current training methods do not reliably search that broader space of programs.
Abstraction is valuable because it exposes structural invariants and reduces the cognitive burden of working directly with low-level implementation detail.
In neural training, the distinction between data and code is blurry because training data effectively programs the model parameters.
